investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Swarm Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-04T12:22–12:29Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No VM was ever assigned, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place any remote-agent pod because the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource was exhausted across the two eligible nodes (0/2 available), and the other four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure: the swarm's peer-pod VM capacity is at or above its limit, preventing any new remote agent from reaching a running/idle/ready state. This is an eval-detected infrastructure condition; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the two peer-pod-capable nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing remote agents or leaked/stuck pods, leaving zero capacity for new scheduling requests. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in all three sibling check failures (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the pod spec targets a label or taint that only matches the two peer-pod nodes, and those nodes are also capacity-exhausted. If the affinity were broadened, the other four nodes might be eligible. Supported by '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' in failed-check.message.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie peer-pod VMs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: prior eval runs or failed agent cleanups may not have released VM resources, artificially inflating consumption. The withCleanup wrapper at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1883 is intended to handle cleanup, but if a prior run crashed before cleanup completed, slots could remain held.

Lower confidence — transient cluster-level resource pressure at the time of the eval run (2026-07-04T12:22–12:29Z): a burst of legitimate remote agent workloads could have temporarily saturated capacity. No traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm or deny this.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: Kata PeerPods VM Capacity Exhausted — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Failing with Unschedulable Pod
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the cluster's 6 nodes have zero available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots (2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm; 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector), causing every remote-agent pod to remain Unschedulable for ~143–146 seconds before the eval timed out. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the runner could not create an agent, and therefore produced zero evidence — leaving all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource capacity across all eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no node can accept a new peer-pod VM at the time of the eval run. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner calls createAgent with type "remote" (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905), which requires a kata peer-pod to be scheduled; when scheduling fails, no agent identity or state is ever returned, so the contract evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) is entirely absent (evidence: expected-output.missing-required-evidence).

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=146159, well within the outageLatencyMs=360000 threshold, confirming the eval did not time out on latency — it failed because the pod was never scheduled.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-266: Contract at line 264 requires [orgId, agentId, readyState, state] — none present because agent creation never completed.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on all eligible nodes: The 2 nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector have no remaining VM slots. This is the direct cause stated in the scheduler message across all three failing checks.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: Four nodes are excluded entirely by the pod's node affinity or node selector configuration, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are also at capacity, no scheduling is possible regardless of VM slot availability elsewhere.

TERTIARY — Peer-pod VM leak or slow cleanup: Previously scheduled remote-agent eval pods or production workloads may not have released their kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, leaving the resource count at zero. The withCleanup wrapper in the runner (run-status-probes.mjs line 1903) is designed to release resources, but if a prior run crashed before cleanup, slots may remain consumed.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — Node pool scaling not triggered: The cluster may lack an autoscaler configured to add nodes with kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, or the autoscaler has not yet responded to the resource pressure.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Swarm Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-04T12:22–12:29Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No VM was ever assigned, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place any remote-agent pod because the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource was exhausted across the two eligible nodes (0/2 available), and the other four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure: the swarm's peer-pod VM capacity is at or above its limit, preventing any new remote agent from reaching a running/idle/ready state. This is an eval-detected infrastructure condition; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable reason with 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on 0/6 nodes, endedAt 2026-07-04T12:27:04.651Z
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable reason with 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on 0/6 nodes, endedAt 2026-07-04T12:29:37.339Z

failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}), confirming no agent lifecycle data was captured
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=153201, which is below the outageLatencyMs threshold of 360000 but the check still failed due to the scheduling error, not a timeout

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never scheduled
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the two peer-pod-capable nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing remote agents or leaked/stuck pods, leaving zero capacity for new scheduling requests. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in all three sibling check failures (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the pod spec targets a label or taint that only matches the two peer-pod nodes, and those nodes are also capacity-exhausted. If the affinity were broadened, the other four nodes might be eligible. Supported by '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' in failed-check.message.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie peer-pod VMs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: prior eval runs or failed agent cleanups may not have released VM resources, artificially inflating consumption. The withCleanup wrapper at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1883 is intended to handle cleanup, but if a prior run crashed before cleanup completed, slots could remain held.

Lower confidence — transient cluster-level resource pressure at the time of the eval run (2026-07-04T12:22–12:29Z): a burst of legitimate remote agent workloads could have temporarily saturated capacity. No traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm or deny this.

If the node affinity or selector on the remote-agent pod spec was found to incorrectly exclude all six nodes (including the two peer-pod nodes), the root cause would shift from capacity exhaustion to a misconfigured pod spec.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: Kata PeerPods VM Capacity Exhausted — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Failing with Unschedulable Pod
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the cluster's 6 nodes have zero available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots (2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm; 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector), causing every remote-agent pod to remain Unschedulable for ~143–146 seconds before the eval timed out. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the runner could not create an agent, and therefore produced zero evidence — leaving all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource capacity across all eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no node can accept a new peer-pod VM at the time of the eval run. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner calls createAgent with type "remote" (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905), which requires a kata peer-pod to be scheduled; when scheduling fails, no agent identity or state is ever returned, so the contract evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) is entirely absent (evidence: expected-output.missing-required-evidence).
proof: failed-check.message: Scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod stuck unscheduled for 143s.
sibling.remote-agent-create: Same Unschedulable message, pod stuck 145s, latencyMs=153201, zero evidence keys.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: Same Unschedulable message, pod stuck 146s, latencyMs=152688, zero evidence keys.
failed-check.evidence: Evidence object is empty — no orgId, agentId, readyState, or state was ever captured.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: All four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are missing, consistent with the agent never being created.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=146159, well within the outageLatencyMs=360000 threshold, confirming the eval did not time out on latency — it failed because the pod was never scheduled.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1897-1905: Runner branch calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1905; a scheduling failure at this step prevents any downstream evidence from being written.
source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-266: Contract at line 264 requires [orgId, agentId, readyState, state] — none present because agent creation never completed.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on all eligible nodes: The 2 nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector have no remaining VM slots. This is the direct cause stated in the scheduler message across all three failing checks.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: Four nodes are excluded entirely by the pod's node affinity or node selector configuration, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are also at capacity, no scheduling is possible regardless of VM slot availability elsewhere.

TERTIARY — Peer-pod VM leak or slow cleanup: Previously scheduled remote-agent eval pods or production workloads may not have released their kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, leaving the resource count at zero. The withCleanup wrapper in the runner (run-status-probes.mjs line 1903) is designed to release resources, but if a prior run crashed before cleanup, slots may remain consumed.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — Node pool scaling not triggered: The cluster may lack an autoscaler configured to add nodes with kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, or the autoscaler has not yet responded to the resource pressure.

followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that polls kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity across all eligible nodes and warns when available slots fall below a configurable threshold (e.g., fewer than 2 free slots), providing early warning before scheduling failures occur.
Add a check that detects pods in Pending/Unschedulable state for more than a configurable duration in the remote-agent namespace, surfacing scheduling pressure before it causes eval timeouts.

Add a post-run cleanup verification eval that confirms no kata.peerpods.io/vm slots remain held by eval-created pods after the withCleanup path completes, catching resource leaks before they accumulate.

Consider adding a pre-flight check at the start of each remote-agent eval run that verifies at least one kata.peerpods.io/vm slot is available before attempting agent creation, allowing the eval to fail fast with a descriptive capacity message rather than waiting for the scheduler timeout.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Exhaustion: kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Insufficient Across All Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in sequence between 12:24 and 12:29 UTC on 2026-07-04 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the requested peer-pod VM because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both were already at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner never received a created agent, and consequently zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were returned, causing a complete contract violation.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource capacity. At the time of the eval run, 0 of 6 nodes could accept a new peer-pod VM: 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm", and 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable on both eligible nodes. Because no VM pod could be scheduled within the eval timeout window (~145–153 s), createAgent() in the eval runner never returned a live agent, and the probe exited with the scheduling error message rather than any response evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to production end-users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes show available (unallocated) VM slots at the time of the failure, the scheduling exhaustion theory would be weakened and a misconfigured node affinity/selector on the pod spec would become the primary suspect.

If the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes also carry kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the pod spec's node selector is incorrect or overly restrictive, the root cause would shift to a pod spec configuration error rather than capacity exhaustion.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeds without any cluster changes, it would suggest a transient scheduling race or a just-released VM slot rather than sustained capacity exhaustion.

If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed in a subsequent run, it would indicate the failure is not a shared VM capacity issue but something specific to the runtime probe's pod spec or timing.
If the cluster shows no kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource defined on any node, the issue would be a missing node label/resource registration rather than capacity exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated capacity on all eligible nodes before attempting remote agent creation, surfacing capacity exhaustion as a distinct check status rather than a scheduling timeout.

Add a VM slot leak detection eval that lists all peer-pod VMs older than a configurable TTL (e.g., 10 minutes) and fails if any are found, catching cleanup failures before they exhaust capacity for subsequent runs.

Add a node affinity coverage eval that verifies at least N nodes match the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector and carry non-zero kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, alerting when the schedulable pool drops below a safe threshold.

Refine the remote-agent-create eval to distinguish between scheduling failures (Unschedulable) and API-level failures, so the failure message can be categorized and routed to the infrastructure team vs. the application team automatically.
